newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey scandal investigation blames government MPs.
newsitem.headline: Turkey scandal investigation blames government MPs.

text.p: A parliamentary investigation into a security scandal accused two Turkish government MPs on Friday of deep involvement in a network of shadowy links between top officials and right-wing gangsters.
"As far as politicians are concerned, Mehmet Agar and Sedat Bucak have been brought to light," inquiry chairman Mehmet Elkatmis told a news conference.
The two deputies are members of the conservative True Path Party (DYP), in coalition with Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists.
Agar resigned as interior minister last November shortly after the scandal broke when a senior policemen and a far-right gangster wanted for murder died in the same car in a traffic accident.
Bucak, who heads a pro-state Kurdish militia, was a passenger in the vehicle.
A prosecutor has officially asked for the pair's parliamentary immunity to be lifted but the request has become caught up in red tape. The MPs deny breaking the law.
